Balita

Peso firms slightly as oil eases

The peso closed a little stronger against the US dollar on Thursday after global oil prices dipped, reports GMA Money: Peso rebounds to P63.665:$1 as oil eases slightly. US crude, the WTI benchmark that helps set oil prices worldwide, fell 0.31% to $83 per barrel. Why does oil move the peso? The Philippines pays for its oil imports in dollars, so cheaper oil means fewer dollars leaving the country. RCBC chief economist Michael Ricafort said the recent sharp rollback (a cut in pump prices at the gas station) could ease inflation and shrink the oil import bill, which supports the peso. "The US dollar/peso exchange rate corrected slightly lower… after slightly lower global crude oil prices," he said. For the family, the move was small: a padala converts into slightly fewer pesos, while cheaper fuel helps the budget at home. Still unknown is whether it holds, since oil prices and global tensions keep swinging. Today's reference rates are in the peso box.

Para sa pamilya: A slightly stronger peso means each dollar sent home buys a bit fewer pesos; check the rate and the fees on the day you send.

US eyes ending green card shortcut for nurses

Filipino nurses and physical therapists hoping for a US green card through an employer could face longer waits under a US Department of Labor proposal, reports GMA Pinoy Abroad: US gov't eyes ending PERM green card process for Filipino nurses, physical therapists. Today, a list called Schedule A lets employers hiring foreign nurses and PTs skip PERM, the labor test where an employer must first show no qualified US worker wants the job. The 107-page proposal, published in the Federal Register, would scrap Schedule A. Employers would generally have to advertise openings for at least 90 days, document their recruitment, and get labor certification before filing a petition. If a qualified US worker applies, the sponsorship may not go through. Immigration attorney Arvin Amatorio warned that hospitals in underserved areas could struggle to fill jobs: "It could be catastrophic for them." Nothing has changed yet. Schedule A remains available under current rules, public comments are open until January 19, 2027, and how much time the new steps would add to each case is still uncertain.

Separately, US Labor Department Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito said in a media interview that his office is investigating major companies over alleged abuse of foreign-worker visa programs. The companies are not named in the coverage. GMA Pinoy Abroad: US gov't eyes ending PERM green card process for Filipino nurses, physical therapists

Para sa pamilya: If a kababayan nurse or PT is being sponsored in the US, ask the employer or lawyer about timing; Schedule A still applies for now.

UBS sees more BSP rate hikes

International bank UBS expects the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to keep raising interest rates, reports Manila Times: UBS sees limited room for monetary easing. "Monetary easing" means cutting rates to make borrowing cheaper. UBS sees another 25-basis-point hike in December and one more in the first quarter of next year (a basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point). That would bring the policy rate, the BSP's benchmark that guides what banks charge on loans, to 6.0 percent. The BSP has already raised rates by a cumulative 125 bps since April to fight inflation, which hit 7.8 percent in October on higher transport and fuel costs. UBS does not expect easing until 2028. On the brighter side, it sees the economy growing 5.1 percent next year, up from 2.1 percent in the third quarter, mainly as public infrastructure spending restarts. This is one bank's forecast. The BSP has not announced its December decision.

UBS senior ASEAN economist Grace Lim said the Philippines is among only two Southeast Asian economies where the bank expects growth to strengthen next year. PhilStar Business: UBS sees Philippines growth rebounding to 5.1% in 2027

Para sa pamilya: Loans that reprice, like some housing, car and salary loans, may stay costly into 2027; ask your lender when your rate is next reviewed.

Diskarte

JoyRide data breach: guard your OTPs

If anyone in the family uses JoyRide, the motorcycle-for-hire app, be extra careful with texts and calls this week. JoyRide confirmed a cyberattack exposed some app data, notified regulators, and asked users never to share one-time passwords (OTPs, the short codes sent to your phone) and not to reply to suspicious texts. Cybersecurity group Deep Web Konek said exposed records include government IDs, addresses and e-wallet information. JoyRide has not confirmed those details, and the full extent is still unknown. PhilStar: JoyRide confirms app data breach

Para sa pamilya: Remind family at home: never give an OTP to anyone, even someone claiming to be from JoyRide, a bank or an e-wallet.
